newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition party to hold poll on army draft.
newsitem.headline: German coalition party to hold poll on army draft.

text.p: The Free Democrats (FDP, junior party in German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition, said on Thursday they would decide this year through a poll of members whether to oppose conscription.
The poll, whose outcome will be binding on party policy, is likely to be held in late autumn, a spokesman for the small liberal party said.

The move was immediately attacked by Defence Minister Volker Ruehe, a member of Kohl's conservative Christian Democrats, who has repeatedly opposed calls for an end to the military draft in recent months.

"Without the conscripts, the efforts on the (flood-stricken region around the River) Oder would never have been possible," Ruehe was quoted as saying in a summary of an interview to appear in Friday's Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper.
Germany's army is composed of around 55 percent career and temporary-contract soldiers and the remainder men conscripted for 10 months service.
Many of Bonn's military allies such as France and the Netherlands have recently given national service its marching orders, but German politicians have been more wary.
Many see the draft as a guarantee that the military retains a close link to civilian society, avoiding the danger of another "state within a state" or a return to Nazi-style militarism.

"The best controls on the army are the conscripts, their parents, their grandparents, friends and relatives -- hundreds of thousands of people who every day of the year control the army from the bottom," Ruehe said.
Calls for a reduction in the size of the army by getting rid of its draft element have increased with the current weakness of German state finances.
